headline: Do the cheap, derivable truth fixes first (host wording, search, a11y, CLS, download hints), then add five optional manifest fields (inputs, outputs, limitations, status, distribution.platforms) with visible 'Not stated' lines and warnings in build/problems.md, never delisting the 6 apps. Other repos need the vendored schema copies, the initialiser, the template Intel opt-out and the app manifests, in that order. Controlled task vocabularies, tiered completeness schemas, per-app host status, example_data, hard requirements and field Core Web Vitals are rejected or deferred.

implement_now.title: One host phrase derived from the plugin's own status (replace hard-coded 'Soon in X')
implement_now.what: In scripts/lcsite/cards.py add one pure function host_phrase(host_key, project_status) used by host_chip (tooltip and sr-only text, cards.py:62-65), host_badge (header, cards.py:68-71) and details_list 'Works in' (pages_apps.py:146-147, 170-173). Status comes from the host's `plugin` repo via data/hosts.yaml -> projects.load_project(...)['status'] (build/sources/*/docs/labconstrictor-project.yaml; all three are 'Experimental' today). Strings: 'napari plugin: experimental', 'napari plugin: available', 'napari plugin: install from GitHub', 'napari plugin: deprecated' (same for Fiji, QuPath); the status text is shown as written and never reworded to a stronger claim. A missing or unknown status stops the build with an error naming the host (no fallback to 'Soon'). It describes the plugin, not a tested claim about the app. Rename the filter label and Details row 'Works in' to 'Also in' / 'Also in (plugins)'. Replace data/site.yaml:8 and pages_site.py:65 by one identical neutral sentence: 'Plugins let apps that declare tools run in napari, Fiji and QuPath; the stage of each plugin is shown on its card.' Update DESIGN.md:32,45,49 and AGENTS.md:29 first, in the same change. Do NOT drop napari/Fiji from the VLab4Mic manifest: the live CellMigrationLab repo has src/vlab4mic_lc_tools; the stale local clone misled one auditor.
implement_now.why: Three labels disagree on one fact: cards say 'Soon in napari', the filter and Details row say 'Works in', the Ecosystem page says Experimental. cards.py:63-71 hard-codes 'Soon'. Confirmed by 4 audit dimensions and the skeptics (verdict: fix the wording, not the filter; never imply per-app testing).
implement_now.tests: Unit test host_phrase for the four statuses plus an unknown status raising an error that names the host; test that card chip, header badge and Details row render the same phrase for one fixture app; update the existing tests at tests/test_site.py:213 and tests/test_design.py:61-62; grep check that the string 'Soon in' no longer exists in scripts/ or data/.

implement_now.title: Additive optional manifest fields: inputs, outputs, limitations, status, distribution.platforms (schema first)
implement_now.what: schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json (schema stays const 1, nothing new is required, the 6 apps stay listed): `inputs`, `outputs`, `limitations`: arrays of 1-6 plain-text strings, 5-200 characters each, description 'A short summary, not README copy; use docs_url for the rest. Say what the app accepts / produces / cannot do.'; `status`: enum Experimental | Available | Deprecated (the same words as schema/labconstrictor-project.schema.json, so the site keeps one maturity vocabulary); `distribution.platforms`: array of enum windows-x86_64, macos-arm64, macos-x86_64, linux-x86_64 ('the systems you support'). Add a schema description for `categories`: 'Words a scientist would search for: synonyms, methods, tools.' Registry: schema/registry-entry.schema.json gets dependentRequired verified_on with verified_version. catalogue.resolve (new small function in a new module scripts/lcsite/completeness.py, <= 30 lines per function) collects WARNINGS only, one line per app in build/problems.md 'Warnings (apps still listed)': missing inputs or outputs for kinds analysis, segmentation, simulation; missing status, quickstart, screenshots for every non-testing app; no licence from the manifest or GitHub. The list of recommended fields is one tuple in config.py that names schema properties so it cannot drift. Warnings never unlist an app. Read optional fields with `in`/optional_list, no `.get(k, default)`. Update content/submit.md: a short Required / Recommended (shown as 'Not stated' when missing) / Optional table, add `categories` to the sample, and a test that the sample manifest validates. scripts/submit_app.py: missing licence is an error in the bot (the Submit page already promises 'has a license'); the recommended-field list is printed as non-blocking warnings. Rollout: publish this schema first, then vendored copies (item 13), then apps.
implement_now.why: No field exists for what a scientist needs before downloading (works with, produces, limits, maturity); the facts exist only in READMEs (CellTracksColab 'Required File Format' CSV or XML, NucleiSky docs/limitations.md, GuessTheCondition .tif layout). Verified with a scratch schema that the 6 current manifests still validate and the current schema rejects the new keys (additionalProperties false). Making them required would delist 6 of 6 apps (0/6 have inputs, outputs, quickstart, docs_url; 1/6 screenshots), which AGENTS.md:62 forbids as a silent exception; BMZ also only warns (FAIR ALERT). Skeptics cut example_data, integrations, requirements.gpu, shows, tiers.
implement_now.tests: Schema tests: all 6 real manifests (from build/snapshot.json) still validate; new fields present/absent/over-length (201 chars, 7 items, bad status, bad platform) with named errors. completeness tests: each warning is produced for the right kinds and never for testing apps, none leaves the app unlisted. Test that the content/submit.md sample validates. Registry test for verified_on dependentRequired. submit_app test: missing licence errors, missing recommended fields only warn.

reject.item: Controlled vocabularies for category/task and a 'What do you want to do?' filter built on them
reject.why: Wrong size for 6 apps: real categories are unique free text, two benchmark examples (Segmentation, Image restoration) match zero apps, NucleiSky does registration not segmentation. Replace it by data-driven filter options (item 2); the only version worth discussing is the deferred `task` cutover.

reject.item: Section 4 'Required' list as hard errors (inputs, outputs, screenshot, quickstart, docs, maintainer, status, limitations)
reject.why: Applied today it delists 6 of 6 apps (quickstart 0/6, docs_url 0/6, authors 0/6, screenshots 1/6, no inputs/outputs/status field), which AGENTS.md:62 and the no-silent-fallback rule forbid. BMZ only warns. Use warnings plus visible 'Not stated' first.

reject.item: Schema 2 or a flag-day with required new fields
reject.why: `schema` is const 1 and legacy aliases are forbidden; additive optional fields in schema 1 are the only compatible route.

reject.item: Three-tier completeness schema (labconstrictor-app.complete.schema.json), 'Description complete' status, hard gate for new submissions
reject.why: Skeptic: all 4 non-testing apps fail 7-9 tier-2 gaps so no real author could pass the bot; a second schema file defines the manifest twice; a 'complete' label reads as a quality mark next to Community/Verified. One recommended-fields tuple with warnings does the job.

reject.item: Verification tier per version, per OS, with date, tester login (`tested` object, 'Install tested' rename)
reject.why: Nobody staffs it: 0 of 6 apps verified, releases ship 4 builds each and are frequent; the procedure is unwritten so the wording would be invented. Keep the binary badge, define it once, show a superseded verification honestly (item 13).

reject.item: Five separate trust panels (availability, status, compatibility, verification, validation)
reject.why: Overbuilt for 6 apps: availability and compatibility are already derived, verification exists, validation is the DOI. Only development status is new and is one optional field.

reject.item: Per-app host integration objects (`integrations`: planned/experimental/usable, tools, tested_with)
reject.why: Host maturity belongs to the three plugins, which all say Experimental and 'untested'; a manifest `usable` would contradict their own guides and repeat one fact in several repos. Derive the wording from the plugin status (item 1).

reject.item: Site-side synonym table; first `categories` entry shown as 'the task'
reject.why: A second hand-maintained description, and the first category is an unordered free list no author ranked. Tokenised search (item 2) fixes the real defect.

reject.item: Core Web Vitals p75 as acceptance criteria, Lighthouse CI, RUM
reject.why: Field metrics this site cannot produce: noindex/Disallow (mkdocs.yml:50), no analytics, no CrUX eligibility; Lighthouse cannot measure INP; adding Node and a live URL breaks 'the build never goes online'. Only lab CLS and image weight are measured and fixed (items 3, 6).

reject.item: `example_data` field, `data_note` on Colab routes, `requirements.gpu`/hardware free text, `shows` enum on screenshots, `doi_kind` now
reject.why: Each adds schema surface for few or zero apps, or asks authors to classify what a caption already says. Example data can be named in a quickstart step or docs_url; hardware needs go in `limitations` if the author states them.

reject.item: Per-app copies of the unsigned-installer warning, Gatekeeper steps, Linux terminal help
reject.why: Already written once in /guides/install/ (template install.md); app pages carry a short hint and a link only (item 9).

reject.item: Benchmark page order B literally (Works with and Produces above Get it with placeholders), and a Get button on App Centre cards
reject.why: With empty fields the placeholders would push the download down on phones; sections render only when the author supplied them. DESIGN.md:40-41 forbids buttons in cards; the route badges already stay visible.
It is a legitimate discriminator (3 apps); the defect is the wording, fixed by item 1 and the data-driven options of item 2.

reject.item: Site-wide statement about what happens to uploaded data for any app, and a site-written 'Intel Macs not supported' line for an app that has not declared it
reject.why: Would be claims the site cannot verify. Only the Colab service facts (account, internet, Google's servers) are written; unsupported platforms come only from the author's distribution.platforms.

reject.item: Dropping napari/Fiji from the VLab4Mic seed on the grounds that its local clone has no lc_tools
reject.why: The local clone is stale; the live CellMigrationLab repo has src/vlab4mic_lc_tools and a manifest with hosts notebook, napari, fiji.

reject.item: Microsoft Store EXE/MSI requirements as an install standard; 30-second timed usability tests with participants; 'nontrivial hardware requirements' as a required field
reject.why: Microsoft needs trusted-root code signing, silent install and immutable URLs the unsigned installers cannot meet; timings need participants and instrumentation; 'nontrivial' cannot be checked by a validator. Use only the listing practice (description, real screenshot).

reject.item: Forcing one global focus ring and removing the phantom fixed div after the footer
reject.why: Both focus styles already meet contrast; the extra stop was seen only in headless Chromium and fixing it blind could break Material's own focus handling.

ask_user.question: Which words should the development `status` field use?
ask_user.recommendation: Reuse the plugin vocabulary (Experimental, Available, Deprecated) so the site has one maturity word list; do not introduce stable/in-development/discontinued.

ask_user.question: May the build only warn (not delist) when inputs, outputs, status, quickstart or screenshots are missing, and from when should the bot require inputs and outputs for new non-testing submissions?
ask_user.recommendation: Warn now; the site stays unlisted (extra.listed false) until the six manifests are filled; consider a hard requirement for new submissions only after the initialiser and template check collect the fields (a decision for later).

ask_user.question: Intel Macs for GuessTheCondition, Playground and VLab4Mic: stop building the Intel .pkg, or keep it and let authors declare distribution.platforms? VLab4Mic's README says both 'ARM64 or Intel' (line 39) and 'Intel Macs are not supported' (line 47).
ask_user.recommendation: Do both: add a documented Intel opt-out in the template workflow (removes the file at the source) and ship distribution.platforms for apps that must keep the asset; ask the VLab4Mic author which sentence is true before anything is declared.

ask_user.question: What does a maintainer actually do to earn 'Verified', and should the badge keep that name?
ask_user.recommendation: Define it as 'a maintainer installed that exact version and ran it on the stated date', keep the word 'Verified' with a visible Community/Verified definition (item 13), and rename or add systems/tester fields only when a real procedure and the first verification exist.

ask_user.question: Who fills in the six apps' own manifests (inputs, outputs, limitations, status, quickstart, screenshots, docs_url, platforms) and who approves the seed-draft wording used for preview?
ask_user.recommendation: The app owners, as six pull requests in their own repos, copying only what their READMEs already say; the site seed drafts stay marked DRAFT and are never presented as author-confirmed.

ask_user.question: Is the replacement of NucleiSky's banner as its only screenshot (by a panel of docs/assets/2D_QC.jpg) acceptable, and may the site hide a banner-style picture from the screenshot slot?
ask_user.recommendation: Yes for the replacement, by the NucleiSky author; the site should not classify images, only render the author's list with caption as alt.

ask_user.question: Is the launch decision (extra.listed false, noindex, Disallow: /) staying until the manifests are filled?
ask_user.recommendation: Keep unlisted until at least the four non-testing apps show Works with, Produces and a real screenshot; then list the site, because discoverability and any field performance data are blocked by that setting.
